grounded_facts: Grant shows recognition of Starla's promise to stay by his side, indicating emotional connection and memory.
memories.memory_text: I saw recognition in Grant's eyes when I reminded him of my promise, like he still remembered us.

grounded_facts: Starla attempts to calm Grant by reminding him of her vow to stay with him.
memories.memory_text: I tried to calm Grant by reminding him that I swore to stay by his side, just like I promised—for better or worse.

grounded_facts: A posse member blocks Grant's path and threatens him with a pistol.
memories.memory_text: I saw one of the posse members step in front of Grant and point a pistol at him, yelling for him to stop.

grounded_facts: Grant violently kills a posse member who blocks his path, escalating the conflict.
memories.memory_text: I watched Grant lash out with something like a tentacle, slicing the man in front of him completely in half—he split open and fell down right before my eyes.

grounded_facts: Bill commands the posse to open fire on Grant after the death of the Good Ol' Boy.
After the death of the Good Ol' Boy, Bill orders the posse to shoot Grant.
memories.memory_text: After that man died, I heard Bill shout 'Fire! Fire!' and then the posse opened fire on Grant while I covered my head.

grounded_facts: A tense standoff between Grant and the posse escalates into violence when Grant kills a posse member and is shot at, leading to his escape and pursuit.
memories.memory_text: I watched the standoff turn violent when Grant killed one of the posse and they started shooting at him, and then he fled into the forest with them chasing after.

grounded_facts: After being shot, Grant releases the cow and flees into the woods.
memories.memory_text: I saw Grant get shot and release the cow before he fled into the woods, and I watched the posse chase after him.

grounded_facts: After hesitating, Starla follows the posse into the forest.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated for a moment, worried and alone, but then I decided to follow them into the forest.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Starla to get away from the dangerous area.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill wave me back and he shouted at me to get out of there, so I knew he wanted me to leave the area right away.

grounded_facts: Margaret shouts to warn Bill of Grant's attack just in time.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margaret shout 'Bill!!' just in time, warning him about Grant's attack.

grounded_facts: Grant, hidden behind a tree, rises and swings a tentacle at Bill, narrowly missing him before retreating.
memories.memory_text: I saw Grant rise from behind a tree and swing a tentacle at Bill, missing him by inches before slithering back into the brush.

grounded_facts: Bill fires his shotgun upward at Grant after dodging the tentacle attack, but Grant has already begun retreating.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Bill fired his shotgun upward at Grant right after dodging the tentacle, but Grant was already retreating.

grounded_facts: After Grant retreats, the posse follows him into the thick brush to continue the chase.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the posse push through the thick brush to follow Grant after he retreated.

grounded_facts: Brenda's body suddenly lurches forward as if something inside is trying to escape, causing the posse to recoil in fear.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brenda's body suddenly lurch forward as if something inside her was trying to burst out, and she screamed in agony — the whole posse, including me, jumped back in fear.

grounded_facts: Bill and Wally discover Brenda transformed into a massive fleshy orb with her head attached, in visible pain and surrounded by rotting animal carcasses.
The group enters the old barn and discovers Brenda in her transformed state, leading to a tense and horrifying confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I entered the barn behind Bill and Wally and saw Brenda transformed into a huge fleshy orb with her head attached, sobbing and in obvious pain, surrounded by rotting carcasses—I was horrified along with the rest of the group.

grounded_facts: Bill suggests taking Brenda to a hospital for help.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill say we should get Brenda to a hospital right away.

grounded_facts: Wally dismisses Bill's idea of going to the hospital.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wally shut down Bill's idea about the hospital, yelling that they wouldn't know what to do with her.

grounded_facts: Brenda screams in pain and begs the group for help as her body begins to tear apart.
memories.memory_text: I heard Brenda screaming for help as her body started to tear apart.

grounded_facts: Starla notices and warns Bill about Brenda's skin starting to split.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brenda's skin starting to split and I called out to Bill to warn him.

grounded_facts: A group gathers in an old barn at night where Brenda undergoes a violent transformation.
memories.memory_text: I was in the barn that night when Brenda started changing violently, and I called out to Bill to do something.

grounded_facts: Bill sees Grant peering into the barn and understands he was manipulated into bringing Brenda to this location.
memories.memory_text: I saw Grant peering in through the window, smiling, and realized he had led us here on purpose.

grounded_facts: Brenda's body ruptures completely, releasing thousands of eyeless parasitic creatures.
The released parasites immediately cover the entire group, overwhelming them.
memories.memory_text: I saw Brenda's skin start to split and tear, then her body burst open completely, spilling thousands of eyeless, slithering parasites that immediately swarmed over all of us before we could react.

grounded_facts: Parasites enter the mouths of Wally, Jack, the Redneck, and the Older Cop, causing violent physical reactions including convulsions and bleeding.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wally gag and convulse after a parasite got into his mouth, and Jack tried to fight one off but it slipped in and he started spitting up blood. I also noticed the Redneck and the Older Cop convulsing, their eyes rolling back and blood coming out as parasites entered them too.

grounded_facts: Bill realizes the danger of parasites entering through the mouth and issues a warning to the group.
memories.memory_text: I think Bill must have realized the mouth was the way in, which is why he shouted that warning and kept protecting me.

grounded_facts: Bill yells a warning to Starla (among others) to keep parasites out of her mouth, contributing to her survival.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill yelling at me and the others not to let the parasites in our mouths, and I felt him swatting them away from my face while he was on top of me.

grounded_facts: A sudden swarm of parasitic creatures attacks the group inside the old barn, attempting to enter their bodies through their mouths.
memories.memory_text: I screamed and covered my mouth when I saw the parasites swarming toward us, trying to get inside. I was knocked down, and one slithered between my lips, but then a knife pinned it to the ground. Bill held me tight and kept shielding me until the creatures finally gave up and slithered away.

grounded_facts: Bill kills a parasite about to enter Starla's mouth and physically protects her by covering her mouth and pressing their bodies together.
Bill uses his body to shield Starla from parasites, covering her mouth and pressing close to prevent entry.
memories.memory_text: I was screaming and tried to cover my mouth when the parasites attacked, but one started slipping in until Bill stabbed it with his knife; then he covered my mouth with his hand and pressed his body against mine, shielding me while the creatures swarmed all over us until they finally gave up.

grounded_facts: After failing to infect Bill and Starla, the parasites abandon their attempts and leave the barn.
memories.memory_text: I felt the parasites give up and slither away after failing to get to me, and when Bill finally took his hand from my mouth, we both looked out the front door of the barn.

grounded_facts: Bill attempts to use his police radio to call for paramedics but fails due to static, indicating lack of communication.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill trying to use his police radio to call for help, and I heard him saying we needed paramedics right away, but all he got back was static—I realized we had no way to reach anyone from the barn.

grounded_facts: Starla checks Wally's pulse and confirms he is still alive, relieving Margaret.
memories.memory_text: I crouched beside Wally, my hands shaking as I checked his pulse, and then I looked at Margaret and nodded to let her know he was still alive.

grounded_facts: Margaret says 'Praise Jesus' upon learning Wally is alive.
memories.memory_text: I heard Margaret say 'Praise Jesus' right after I confirmed Wally was alive.

grounded_facts: Trevor responds to Margaret's 'Praise Jesus' with sarcasm, calling it excessive given the situation.
memories.memory_text: I heard Trevor respond to Margaret's 'Praise Jesus' with sarcasm, saying it was excessive.

grounded_facts: Trevor asks Margaret and Starla if they have ever seen or heard of creatures like the ones that attacked.
memories.memory_text: I remember Trevor asking if any of us had ever seen or heard of creatures like the ones that attacked, and I shook my head when he looked at me.

grounded_facts: After failing to get radio reception, Bill decides to go to his car to call for help, taking responsibility for the mission.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill say he'd go to his car to call for help after the radio didn't work, taking it on himself to handle it.

grounded_facts: A tense gathering in the barn after a violent incident, where survivors assess injuries and plan emergency response.
memories.memory_text: I was standing in the barn with Trevor and Margaret, still shaken from what had just happened, when I saw Bill struggling with the radio. I nodded to Margaret to let her know Wally was alive, and when Bill started to leave, I grabbed him to tell him I’d run to his car to call for paramedics.

grounded_facts: Starla grabs Bill and tells him to be careful as he leaves, showing emotional support.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed Bill and told him to be careful as he left, because I was worried about him.

grounded_facts: Bill leaves the barn and jogs into the forest toward his car to call for help.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill leave the barn and jog into the forest toward his car to call for help.

grounded_facts: Wally, previously sick and unconscious, sits up and approaches Starla with milky eyes, speaking in Grant's cadence and expressing remorse with philosophical justifications for his actions.
Wally speaks to Starla using Grant's speech patterns, apologizing for his violent actions while justifying them as expressions of nature, creating emotional and psychological distress.
memories.memory_text: I saw Wally sit up with milky eyes and step toward me in the dark, and when he spoke, it was in Grant's voice—soft and familiar—apologizing for strangling me and killing the pets, saying he couldn't help it because it was his nature, and I felt frozen, like I couldn't breathe or move.

grounded_facts: Margaret is hit by a yellowish stream of infectious fluid ('gleek') from the Redneck's mouth, which burns and begins to grotesquely mutate her hand.
The Redneck recruit spits infectious 'gleek' onto Margaret's hand, causing immediate and severe tissue damage.
memories.memory_text: I saw the Redneck open his mouth and shoot a yellowish stream of fluid that hit Margaret's hand, burning her and making her scream as her skin started to twist and mutate.

grounded_facts: Jack spits 'gleek' onto Margaret's neck, causing rapid swelling that obstructs her breathing and leads to death.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Jack spits 'gleek' onto Margaret's neck, causing rapid swelling that obstructs her breathing and leads to death.

grounded_facts: The Older Cop physically removes and eats part of Margaret's neck flesh as she dies.
memories.memory_text: I remember that The Older Cop physically removes and eats part of Margaret's neck flesh as she dies.

grounded_facts: After being gleecked on the neck by Jack, Margaret suffocates as her neck swells; the Older Cop then eats part of her neck flesh as she dies.
memories.memory_text: I remember that After being gleecked on the neck by Jack, Margaret suffocates as her neck swells; the Older Cop then eats part of her neck flesh as she dies.

grounded_facts: The infected posse, speaking in unison with Grant's cadence, demands that Starla obey them and put down her weapon.
memories.memory_text: I heard the infected posse speaking in unison, demanding I obey them and put down my weapon, their voices echoing with a cadence that felt both foreign and terrifyingly familiar.

grounded_facts: Starla shoots Wally in the face, killing him and causing a parasite to emerge from his head wound and flee into the woods.
Starla shoots Wally in the face with a rifle, killing him and causing a parasite to emerge from his skull.
memories.memory_text: I shot Wally in the face with my rifle, killing him, and I saw a parasite squirm out of the wound in his skull and flee into the woods.

grounded_facts: An intense confrontation at an old barn at night, where the infected posse attacks Margaret, kills her, and is subsequently challenged by Starla, leading to violence and escape.
memories.memory_text: I watched the infected posse attack Margaret and Trevor by the old barn, and when the Redneck gleecked Margaret, I grabbed the rifle and shot Wally in the face to stop them, but then I realized I had no more ammo and had to flee with Trevor.

grounded_facts: After running out of ammo, Starla and Trevor flee from the infected posse as they charge at them.
memories.memory_text: I ran out of ammo and saw the infected posse charging at us, so Trevor and I turned and fled as fast as we could.

grounded_facts: Trevor and Starla run in a panicked zigzag pattern through a densely wooded area at night.
memories.memory_text: I ran in a panicked zigzag through the dark woods with Trevor, dodging trees as we both gasped for breath, trying to get away from whatever was chasing us.

grounded_facts: Jack is positioned right behind Starla, indicating close physical pursuit or accompaniment.
memories.memory_text: I looked back and saw Jack right behind me, so close that I could feel his presence pressing in.

grounded_facts: Starla trips over old, fallen barbed wire fencing on the forest floor, becoming aware of its presence.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Starla trips over old, fallen barbed wire fencing on the forest floor, becoming aware of its presence.

grounded_facts: Jack grabs Starla's blouse and screeches furiously, physically attacking her.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Jack grabs Starla's blouse and screeches furiously, physically attacking her.

grounded_facts: Jack, who was attacking Starla, lets go of her when he hears and sees Bill's approaching police car.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Jack, who was attacking Starla, lets go of her when he hears and sees Bill's approaching police car.

grounded_facts: Starla stabs Jack in the neck with a rusty stake from the barbed wire fence, causing him to fall over dead.
memories.memory_text: I rose behind Jack, grabbed a rusty stake from the barbed wire fence, and thrust it into his neck—he turned to look at me before falling over dead.

grounded_facts: Trevor and Starla enter Bill's police car and drive away with the Older Cop and Redneck approaching.
memories.memory_text: I got into Bill's police car with Trevor and we started to drive away as the Older Cop and the Redneck were approaching.

grounded_facts: As the police car backs away, the Older Cop yells Starla's name.
memories.memory_text: As we backed away, I heard the Older Cop yell my name.

grounded_facts: A violent encounter in the forest at night involving Starla, Jack, and Bill's arrival in a police car, culminating in Jack's death and the group's escape.
memories.memory_text: I remember that A violent encounter in the forest at night involving Starla, Jack, and Bill's arrival in a police car, culminating in Jack's death and the group's escape.

grounded_facts: The police car emerges from the forest, visibly damaged, beginning the return journey toward town.
memories.memory_text: I was in the police car as it pulled out of the forest, and I remember how damaged it looked and how we all sat there in a daze, still trying to process everything.

grounded_facts: Bill attempts to contact Shelby via police radio but initially receives no response, causing concern among the group.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill call out to Shelby over the radio, but all we got was static, and I could feel the worry building in the room.

grounded_facts: Bill uses the police radio to attempt contact with Shelby, first unsuccessfully, then successfully.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill grab the police radio and try to reach Shelby, calling out twice before finally getting a response.

grounded_facts: Shelby responds to Bill's call, confirming communication is restored, bringing relief to Bill and Starla.
memories.memory_text: I felt the tension break when Shelby's voice came through the radio, and I shared a look with Bill—I could see the relief in his eyes, and I know he saw it in mine.

grounded_facts: Starla confirms Kylie's claim by stating they saw a parasite emerge from Wally's head.
memories.memory_text: I confirmed what Kylie said because we saw a parasite come out of Wally's head.

grounded_facts: Kylie explains that the parasites are part of Mrs. Grant's husband, an entity that travels between worlds, takes over hosts, and spreads through worm-like forms.
memories.memory_text: I was told the parasites are part of Mrs. Grant's husband, an entity that travels between worlds, takes over hosts, and spreads through worm-like forms.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Kylie if stopping Mr. Grant would stop the parasite threat.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill ask if stopping Mr. Grant would stop the parasite threat.

grounded_facts: The police car suddenly stops functioning and comes to a halt, stranding the group.
memories.memory_text: I was in the police car when it started chugging and then slowed down until it came to a complete stop, leaving us stranded.

grounded_facts: The group's car breaks down on Route 22, one mile outside Wheelsy, forcing them to continue on foot.
memories.memory_text: I stepped out of the car with the others when it broke down on Route 22, just a mile outside Wheelsy, and I could see we'd have to walk.

grounded_facts: Bill retrieves his satchel of weapons from the trunk; Trevor takes ammo to reload his pistol.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill pull his satchel of weapons from the trunk, and Trevor took some ammo to reload his pistol right there on the road.

grounded_facts: Bill contacts Shelby via radio and instructs her to leave her post to pick them up.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill call Shelby on the radio and tell her to leave her post to come pick us up after we got stranded.

grounded_facts: The group walks down the road toward the town of Wheelsy after their car breaks down.
memories.memory_text: I walked down the road toward Wheelsy with the group, and Bill and I were leading the way.

grounded_facts: Bill asks Starla why she married Grant, expressing curiosity about her past relationship.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill asking me why I married Grant, saying he was curious because it never seemed like it was out of love.

grounded_facts: Starla reveals the traumatic abuse by her father and how Grant intervened violently, leading to her marriage for protection rather than love.
memories.memory_text: I told Bill about how my father abused me from a young age and how Grant found out, beat him with a tire iron, and that’s why I married him — because I finally felt safe, and that was the closest thing to love I ever knew.

grounded_facts: Bill admits he has always regretted not running away with Starla to Hollywood.
memories.memory_text: I remember Bill telling me he always regretted not running away with me to Hollywood.

grounded_facts: A sudden ambush by multiple diseased deer on the group as they investigate an abandoned car on the road.
memories.memory_text: I saw diseased deer coming at us from different directions when we were checking out the abandoned car.

grounded_facts: Kylie flees under a rock overhang to escape the attacking deer.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kylie scream and dive under a rock overhang to get away from the attacking deer.

grounded_facts: A diseased deer attacks Bill, knocking him down and preventing him from reaching his shotgun.
memories.memory_text: I saw a diseased deer knock Bill down and keep him from reaching his shotgun while another one bit into his shoulder.

grounded_facts: Starla runs toward the abandoned Buick to escape a horned buck but is bitten and dragged.
memories.memory_text: I ran toward the abandoned Buick to escape a horned buck, and even though he bit my ankle and started dragging me, I grabbed the steering wheel and held on with all my might.

grounded_facts: A diseased deer knocks Trevor down and stomps on his ribs, then bites his sleeve and forces him to drop his pistol.
memories.memory_text: I saw a diseased deer knock Trevor down, stomp on his ribs, and bite his sleeve so hard he dropped his pistol.

grounded_facts: Kylie crawls out from cover and pushes Bill's shotgun toward him, enabling him to fight back.
Kylie pushes Bill's shotgun within his reach while he is under attack.
memories.memory_text: I saw Kylie crawl out from under the rock overhang and push Bill's shotgun within his reach while he was trying to fight off the attack.

grounded_facts: While being pulled by the horned buck, Starla turns the ignition and starts the Buick's engine, then presses the gas.
memories.memory_text: I was being pulled by the horned buck, but I managed to turn the ignition and start the Buick's engine, then I pressed the gas to wrench myself free.

grounded_facts: Bill uses his shotgun to kill the tumorous doe biting into his leg after regaining it with Kylie's help.
memories.memory_text: I saw the tumorous doe leap onto Bill and bite into his leg, and I watched as he managed to get his shotgun free and shove it into the deer before pulling the trigger, ending it.

grounded_facts: Bill shoots and hits the deer that is dragging Trevor down the road.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill stand up and shoot at the deer that was dragging Trevor down the road—he missed the first shot but hit it on the second try.

grounded_facts: Starla pulls herself into the driver's seat, backs up, and opens the passenger door to let others in.
memories.memory_text: I pulled myself into the driver's seat, backed up alongside my friends, and threw open the passenger door.

grounded_facts: Starla opens the passenger door and shouts for the others to get in the car.
memories.memory_text: I opened the passenger door and shouted 'Get in!' to call the others to safety.

grounded_facts: An SUV crashes violently into the side of the Buick, forcing it backward into a flower store's storefront.
memories.memory_text: I saw an SUV barreling toward us before it slammed into the side of the Buick and smashed us backward across a lot, right through the glass storefront of a flower store.

grounded_facts: Kylie dies from the car crash, her neck severely broken.
memories.memory_text: I looked back at Kylie and saw that her neck was bent at a terrible angle, bone sticking out of her skin—I knew she was gone.

grounded_facts: Starla struggles out of the wrecked car and falls onto the broken glass and water-covered floor.
memories.memory_text: I struggled to get out of the car and when I finally did, I fell onto the floor covered in broken glass and water.

grounded_facts: Starla uses a metal bar to violently kill the diseased driver who approaches her.
memories.memory_text: I saw the diseased driver lurching toward me, ready to grab me, so I grabbed a metal bar and slammed it into his shin. I crawled on top of him and kept bringing it down on his head over and over, shouting and crying, until I saw he was very dead.

grounded_facts: Dozens of diseased townspeople emerge and advance toward Starla, recognizing her.
memories.memory_text: I looked up and saw dozens of diseased townspeople coming toward me, emerging from between the buildings, and I knew they had seen me.

grounded_facts: The immediate aftermath of a car crash in a destroyed flower store, with survivors dealing with death and incoming threats.
memories.memory_text: I struggled to get out of the car and fell onto the floor, surrounded by broken glass and water, then saw a dead man and realized dozens of diseased townsfolk were coming straight for me.

grounded_facts: The diseased townsfolk shout Starla's name as they approach, indicating recognition and likely hostile intent.
memories.memory_text: I heard them shouting my name, 'Starrrrrlaaaaaa!!', as they advanced, and I realized they recognized me and meant to harm me.

grounded_facts: Bill and Trevor, injured but mobile, approach Starla and pull her toward safety.
memories.memory_text: I felt Bill and Trevor grab me and pull me toward a back door while I was still dazed from the crash.

grounded_facts: Bill tells Starla to come on as they pull her toward the back door.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill tell me to come on as they pulled me toward the back door.

grounded_facts: Trevor voices fear and uncertainty about their situation upon seeing the parasites.
memories.memory_text: I heard Trevor shout, 'What the hell are we going to do?!' when he saw the parasites, and his fear made my own hands shake as I aimed my gun.

grounded_facts: Bill instructs Trevor to block the doors as a defensive measure against the parasites.
memories.memory_text: I heard Bill tell Trevor and me to block the doors however we could to keep the parasites out.

grounded_facts: Starla shows skepticism about the effectiveness of their barricading efforts but still participates.
memories.memory_text: I looked at the barricade and doubted it would really keep them out, but I helped anyway.

grounded_facts: Bill and Trevor attempt to barricade the storeroom doors to keep out parasites by nailing metal shelving and other materials over them.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill and Trevor start nailing metal shelving and other stuff over the doors to barricade them in the storeroom.

grounded_facts: Slithering parasites begin to enter the storeroom through cracks in the walls and corners, prompting immediate defensive action.
memories.memory_text: I saw slithering parasites coming in through cracks in the walls and corners of the storeroom, and that's when we knew we had to act fast.

grounded_facts: Trevor, then Bill and Starla, open fire on the invading parasites with firearms, causing dust and reduced visibility.
memories.memory_text: I opened fire along with Trevor and Bill when the parasites started coming in, and the dust from all the shooting made it hard to see anything around us.

grounded_facts: A desperate attempt by Bill, Trevor, and Starla to defend themselves from invading parasites in a flower store storage area.
memories.memory_text: I was right there with Bill and Trevor, desperately fighting off the parasites that slithered in through cracks in the room, even as dust from the gunfire made it hard to see.

grounded_facts: After running out of ammunition, Bill uses an electric circular saw to physically attack and cut apart the parasites.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill run out of ammo and grab an electric circular saw to start cutting apart the parasites with it.

grounded_facts: Starla decides to let the diseased take her in order to lead them away and create an escape opportunity.
Starla informs Bill of her plan to let herself be taken so he can follow and kill the leader.
memories.memory_text: I decided to let the diseased take me because I knew their leader wanted me, and I told Bill he could follow me and kill the leader while I led them away.

grounded_facts: Bill reacts with shock and refusal when Starla announces her plan to surrender.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill react with shock and he refused when I told him my plan, shouting 'No, Starla! No!'

grounded_facts: A group of diseased townspeople violently break into the storage area of a flower store, leading to death and escape attempts.
memories.memory_text: I witnessed the diseased violently break into the flower store's storage area, bursting through the wall and overwhelming Trevor with their attacks.

grounded_facts: Trevor is overwhelmed by the diseased, doused in corrosive liquid, and torn apart.
memories.memory_text: I saw Trevor get hit by the diseased, doused in that burning liquid, and torn apart right in front of me while Bill tried to pull him free.

grounded_facts: Bill shoots two diseased people who attack him and Starla, then flees across the street.
memories.memory_text: I saw Bill shoot the two diseased people who came screaming at us, and then he ran across the street to escape.

grounded_facts: Starla motions with her head for Bill to run, refusing to follow him despite his expectation.
memories.memory_text: I stayed in place and didn't follow Bill, even though he expected me to—I looked down and then motioned with my head for him to go without me.

grounded_facts: Multiple diseased townspeople simultaneously voice personal betrayals and emotional pain toward Starla, attributing their suffering to her actions and Grant's legacy.
The infected townspeople voice deep-seated emotional accusations toward Starla, rooted in jealousy, betrayal, and inherited pain from Grant.
memories.memory_text: I was surrounded by the diseased townspeople who all began wailing at once, their voices full of pain, jealousy, and betrayal, blaming me and Grant's legacy for their suffering.

grounded_facts: Starla attempts to redirect the confrontation by asking to speak with 'Grant's more real face', implying a desire to engage the core identity behind the collective manifestation.
memories.memory_text: I tried to calm things down by asking to speak with Grant's more real face, hoping to reach whoever was really in control.

grounded_facts: A group of diseased townspeople confront Starla outside a flower store, expressing collective emotional trauma and ultimately capturing her.
memories.memory_text: After Bill left, I was surrounded by the diseased townspeople who screeched and wailed at me, their voices full of pain and anger, and I felt a dog licking my leg before one of them grabbed my face and they all pulled me in and started dragging me away.

grounded_facts: After attempting to negotiate, Starla is physically seized and dragged away by the diseased townsfolk.
memories.memory_text: I was grabbed and dragged away by the diseased townsfolk, even though I wasn't fighting them.

grounded_facts: Starla remains behind while Bill flees, allowing the diseased townsfolk to encircle and seize her without resistance.
memories.memory_text: I stayed behind while Bill ran, and I just stood there, staring at the ground as the townsfolk closed in around me and then seized me without resistance.

grounded_facts: Starla falls to her hands and knees after being pushed too hard by one of the diseased; she struggles to get back up while continuing to be pressured by the group.
memories.memory_text: I was pushed hard by one of the diseased and fell to my hands and knees, and they kept pressing on me—I struggled to get back up, but I managed to stumble to my feet and keep moving, even though I could barely catch my breath.

grounded_facts: Starla is forced by the diseased to approach and then slowly enter the dark house.
memories.memory_text: I was pushed by the diseased to the front door, and when I saw the dark hole of the house, I stopped and looked back at their rotting faces before I slowly went in.

grounded_facts: Starla discovers the transformed garage and foyer into a feeding area with rotten meat and bodies.
memories.memory_text: I balked at the awful smell when I entered the foyer, then saw the garage wall had been torn out—rotten meat and bodies piled up inside, this was Grant's feeding area. I called out, 'Grant?'

grounded_facts: Starla discovers a meat thermometer among scattered kitchen supplies and decides to keep the metal spike.
memories.memory_text: I spotted a meat thermometer among the scattered utensils on the floor, picked it up, broke off the top, and kept the metal spike by hiding it in the seam of my skirt.

grounded_facts: The song 'Every Woman in the World' begins playing through tinny speakers, evoking a shared memory with Grant.
memories.memory_text: I heard 'Every Woman in the World' start playing through the speakers, and it brought back the memory of dancing with Grant.

grounded_facts: Upon hearing the music and seeing part of Grant above, Starla initiates communication.

memories.memory_text: I stepped slow toward that deer, talking soft—'It's okay, sweetheart'—and she actually calmed down enough for me to yank the cord from the wall without her kicking me in the head.
After she bolted with that phone still tied to her leg, I said, 'Hell, she took a phone. Now them forest critters are gonna be calling us all hours of the night,' and everyone cracked up.
I told Starla about the spot on the bluffs where the town lights look like a kaleidoscope when the fog rolls in just right—only a few of us know how to get there.

I asked Starla if she knew Brenda Gutierrez, and when she said no, I told her Brenda disappeared Friday night and that Grant was the last one seen with her at the Deer Cheer — I could see it hit her, the way her face changed.
I handed Starla my card and told her to have Grant call me right away — my hand was steady, but I could feel the urgency in my voice, and she just nodded, looking shaken.
I stood by the bulletin board, pointing to each red circle as I laid out the pattern—Raglans' ranch, then Fitzgibbon's, then the Castavets'. The posse was quiet, actually listening.
I pointed to the next red circle and said the Strutemyers' ranch would be hit next—if the pattern held. Then I told them we had to move tonight, lie low, and wait.
I remember Starla knocking on my window late at night when she was twelve, asking me to run away with her to Hollywood because she needed a bodyguard—I was in ROTC, and she thought I was her ticket.

I saw Brenda—her head weeping, stuck to this huge pulsing mass of flesh, screaming and lurching like something inside her was fighting to get out. She was sobbing, covered in blood, surrounded by rotting animals and flies.

She asked me for possum meat, smiling at me like I was her daddy, trying to charm me—her voice pleading, hungry. I couldn't move. The thing she'd become just sat there, starving, asking for scraps at my feet.
I saw Brenda's skin split open, one tear after another, and heard her screaming like nothing I'd ever heard—then her whole body burst, spilling those slugs everywhere.
Right after I saw the tears in her skin start, I looked to the window—and saw Grant watching, smiling. That's when I knew he brought us here on purpose.
I looked down at Brenda's body—her skin torn open, bones twisted and sticking out, like something ripped her apart from the inside. It wasn't just death; it was like she'd been used and discarded.

I turned and saw them moving—parasites swarming like a living tide, shaking the brush as they rushed into the forest. I couldn't tell how many there were, but they were fast, and they were getting away.

I shouted 'Hey!' when I saw the Strutemyers smashing the truck with rocks, and they stopped and turned toward me—something was wrong with them, their eyes, their skin. Then Kylie came running past them, crying, and grabbed onto me like I was the only thing keeping her upright.

The rancher with the cleft palate came out of nowhere, swung a shovel, and knocked me down—I felt the shotgun beside me in the dirt, yanked the trigger, and the blast took him in the foot. I grabbed Kylie and ran as more of them charged through the field.
I went to reload my shotgun, but then it hit me—ammo's in the trunk. No way to get to it now.
I grabbed the police radio and called out for Trevor and Margaret—no idea if they heard me over the static.

I heard Kylie screaming at me to go, but I couldn't leave Trevor and the others behind—I turned the car up onto the ranch and drove back into the swarm, my hands tight on the wheel, mud spraying as the engine roared.
I backed the car out from between the trees, saw the older cop and that redneck closing in, and yelled for Trevor and Starla to get in—no time to waste.
I was on the ground, one of those deer on top of me, tearing into my leg—I couldn't reach my rifle until I saw Kylie push it just within my grasp.
I swung the rifle like a bat into the deer's face, then flipped it around and shot the one biting me—felt the kick as the muzzle blew her apart.
I grabbed the hammers and nails off the bench—first thing I saw that could block the doors. Nailed anything we could over the frames, same as Trevor and Starla.
Ran out of ammo fast—dust everywhere, couldn't see straight. I grabbed that electric circular saw, fired it up, and started jamming it into the things crawling in. They squeaked when it cut through.
I grabbed Trevor's wrist, trying to pull him back, but his body just tore apart in my hands—his flesh turned soft and split like wet paper, and I was left holding only his arm.
I shot the two diseased people when they came screeching at us, then ran across the street. I turned, but Starla didn't follow.
I turned back and saw Starla just standing there, not moving, with tears in her eyes—she told me to go without her, and I didn’t understand why she stayed as they surrounded her.
I pressed myself into the crevice of the building, holding still as those infected passed close by, calling out names like they were hunting prey.
After they moved on, I peeked toward the next street and saw them dragging Starla—I made sure the coast was clear before following.
I stepped into the kid's room, all planes and trophies on the walls, and checked my shotgun was loaded before edging up to the window frame to watch the Grant bedroom—window shut tight, no way in.
I heard Starla scream 'Now, Bill!! Kill the motherfucker!!' after she stabbed Grant in the eyes and forehead with that metal spike.
I fired through the window, emptying the whole clip into Grant—glass shattered, bullets hit, but he didn't go down.
Hands grabbed me from all sides—townspeople, fast and strong. Then something wrapped around my neck, lifting me off the ground while Grant screamed.
I found a Nissan Maxima just sitting in the street, keys still in the ignition—called Starla over fast, didn't waste a second.
I grabbed Starla's hand when I saw her tearing up watching those people through the window — she squeezed back so hard it almost hurt.
She said we could get first aid and food at the gas station up ahead, and I told her yeah, that was good — kept it simple, but I meant it.
I begged Starla, told her I’d try not to hurt anyone—my voice was raw, desperate—then said those words, 'It’s my nature,' like I was handing her the truth I’d been running from.
I saw the tears on her face, the gun steady in her hands, and then she said, 'And this is mine'—a second before the gunshot cracked out, loud and final.
I was in the car, then the door flew open and I was kicked out, sliding hard across the pavement.

memories.memory_text: I saw the wedding photo on my desk start to shake, then noticed the guys in the workshop almost dropping that glass pane—just a tremor, I told them, trying to keep things calm while I went back to my files.
I remember snapping at Starla about that call—'Callin' for you. What the hell?'—and shoving a bite of food in my mouth like I could bite through the anger too.

I told her to flip, then flipped her nipple through her nightgown—just trying to get a reaction. When she called it disrespectful and I saw her look scared, something in me snapped. I had to get out.
I bent down to get a closer look at that pulsing yellow thing, and before I knew it, a thin spore shot out and hit me right in the gut—sharp, like a sting.
I saw the spore wriggle into my skin and vanish under my flesh—then this burning surge shot up my body, like something crawling inside me, taking hold.
I saw my face in the mirror and pulled at the skin, staring close—my eyes lit up, and I smiled at what I saw.
I crept to the bathroom door and peeked around—Starla was under the water, soaping herself, and I just watched, tilted my head, couldn't look away.
I held Starla close, slow dancing in the candlelight, my voice breaking as I called her sugarplum and swore I’d change—tears in my eyes, feeling her warmth against me again.
She touched my stomach and froze—I saw her eyes lock onto the wound, yellow and veined; I yanked my shirt down fast, calling it just a bug bite, but I felt her shock.
I was standin' there lookin' at them rib eyes, thinkin' 'bout the dinner party, and I said fourteen—that felt right, bold but not crazy.
Then I just snapped—told the butcher to give me every last rib eye, then started grabbin' chicken wings, pork loins, even that fancy osso buco... like I couldn't stop myself.
I was moving the meat around, just feeling it under my hands, when something skittered near the pile—I looked, and there it was, a rat chewing on the ribs. Then it hit me: you're meat. Just meat.
The rat tried to get away, but I grabbed it fast—felt it squirming and biting my hand, squeaking like it mattered. I snapped its neck and threw it onto the pile. Just more meat now.
I called her my princess, smiled at her—she was confused but I made it sound sweet, like the locks were for her birthday present, something special I had to keep safe.
I watched her walk up the stairs, her body moving ahead of me, and it hit me—clear as anything—she's just meat, that's all she is.
I spread the plants out just right, fluffed them up soft—felt good to make it mine, to sit back and see it done. No one watching, just me, and that quiet joy in my chest.

I saw Starla sitting on the bed, putting on her nylons, not knowing I was there—I stared at her neck, her ear, and then something started pushing up under my shirt, this writhing thing coming out of my stomach, pointing at her.
I turned away from her, trying to push the thing back in, and when she asked what I was doing, I just said she was pretty—my voice sounded strange, even to me.
I saw that kid wave at Starla, and I grabbed her arm—had to make sure she knew he wasn't welcome. She said he was just a student, but I don't trust the way he looked at her.
I turned toward her after taking my shirt off, and I saw her face—her eyes went wide when she saw the thing on my stomach, that pulsing spout covered in blue moss, veins writhing like it was alive.
I pinned her wrists to the rock, my hand over her mouth, and I watched the tubule push into her stomach—she was crying, trembling, then going stiff as the fluid pumped in.
I was holding Starla from behind, half-asleep, just trying to stay close to her, but I didn’t know she was looking at the dirt on my pants.

I saw the fear in Starla's eyes when she looked at my face—those pustules I can feel crawling under my skin—and I laughed it off, told her it was just a bee sting, but I could barely stand straight and my body's falling apart.
I shoved the meat into the garbage bag in the dark, making sure it was hidden—couldn't risk anyone seeing what I was doing.

I dumped the bag of rotting meat and dead animals in front of her, told her I’d been saving it for a rainy day. She was starving, gagging, begging—then just stared at it like she didn’t know whether to scream or drool.

She looked up at me, scared, said she was sorry, wanted to go to a hospital—like that was even an option. I didn’t say anything. Just watched. Then she reached down and grabbed that maggoty pork chop, started eating like an animal.
I saw her turn toward the window, not knowing it was me—really seeing me—and then her face froze when she finally did.
I couldn't hold it in—I let out a roar and vanished into the dark before she could scream again.
I was crying, my breath ragged and wet, telling her I loved her—really telling her—while the thing in my chest pulsed and the tubule reached under her shirt, trying to get inside.
I had her from behind, my arm locking around her throat like a coil, cutting off her breath—then the door slammed, guns fired, and I felt the burn of a bullet before I vanished into the dark.
I feel my body twisting, breaking down—like I’m not me anymore, just this pulsing mass crawling out of the trees, and I know they’re watching but I can’t stop, I don’t even have a face to show them.

I saw Starla coming toward me, saying it’s okay, that she’d stay by my side—her voice soft like before, but I could smell the fear on her, feel the eyes of the others closing in, guns ready. My breath was heavy, wet, wrong, and when she said 'remember,' I did, but the words burned in my chest like they didn’t belong.

The man stepped in front of me, gun out, talking tough—I didn’t hear the rest. I snapped the tentacle forward, felt it slice through him clean, watched his two halves stare down before he dropped. Then the shots came, burning into me, and I dropped the cow and ran, slithering into the dark while bullets cracked behind me.
I saw Starla leaning in like she was going to kiss me, and I felt that rush—joy, maybe—before she jammed the spike into my eye.
After the first stab, I was screaming and thrashing, blind—then I felt the spike slam into my other eye, and finally driven hard into my forehead.
I felt the bullets hit me, but there was no pain—just the glass breaking around me as I kept moving down the stairs.
I lashed out with my tentacle, felt it coil around his neck, and lifted him up while the others held him—my scream tore through the night.
I felt my body tear apart from the inside, and then I was gone.

memories.memory_text: I pushed him off me and said, 'That's disrespectful'—my voice was quiet but I meant it, and he actually stopped and got off the bed.
I stayed still, watching him put on his slacks and leave—I couldn't move, just felt the dark and the silence and how afraid I was.

I was standing there in just a towel, and he took my hand, pulled me close, started slow dancing with me—just like on our wedding day, he said, his voice breaking. I could see the tears in his eyes when he apologized, and I nodded because I felt it too, that old softness pulling me back.

My hand was on his stomach, moving over his skin like before, and then I felt it—something wrong, a strange spot. I froze, looked down, and saw that yellow wound, veins spreading around it like roots. He covered it fast, said it was just a bug bite, but it didn’t look like any bite I’d ever seen.

I pressed the garage door opener, but it just shuddered and stayed shut—I didn’t understand at first, until I got out and saw the padlock bolted to the ground. That’s when I knew he didn’t want me back.

I reached for the garage door and felt this cold, new lock under my fingers—shiny, out of place. I didn’t understand why Grant would lock me out of my own house, not until he said it was to hide a 'super-special birthday present' and called me his princess like that was supposed to make it okay.

I was already walking away, trying to pretend everything was normal, when I heard him mutter 'You're meat'—flat, like he wasn’t even talking to me. When I turned, he blinked like he’d woken up, said it was nothing, but his eyes had changed, and I felt... exposed.
I swung the bat at the lock, grunting with each hit, feeling the jolt in my hands until the lock finally broke free.
When I opened the door, that awful stench hit me so hard I covered my face, terrified, but I still stepped inside.
I saw Roscoe on the floor, his tongue hanging out, surrounded by all those dead animals sorted like meat—dogs, cats, labeled like it meant nothing. I couldn’t stop the tears, I just ran back inside.
I felt that thing from his chest slither under my shirt and poke into my skin—I grabbed the table leg and smashed him in the head just to get free.
He came from behind and wrapped his arm around my neck like a snake—I couldn’t breathe, my face was turning purple, and I could hear the door slamming but couldn’t call out.
I stood up, my legs shaking, and walked out of the barn into the dark — I could feel Bill's eyes on me, but I didn't stop.

I moved close to Grant, my voice soft but firm, telling him it was okay—that he was just sick and I’d stay by his side, like I swore I would. For better or worse. I saw in his eyes that he remembered, that he heard me.

I saw Grant snap out a tentacle and split the man in half. His body opened up, and he looked down before falling. Then the posse started shooting. Grant screeched, let go of the cow, and ran into the forest.

I told Grant about my father that day at the gas station, the first time I ever said it out loud—how he beat me, how it got worse when I was older. I remember the way Grant looked when he saw my swollen lip, the way he just... stopped.
Grant picked up the tire iron and went into the garage after my father. I didn't stop him. I just stood there, shaking. That was the first time I ever felt someone was protecting me—like I mattered.

I remember the impact—metal screaming, glass exploding around me, and then the world flipping as we crashed through the storefront. I was still inside the car, trapped, surrounded by shattered glass and the smell of gasoline.
I looked over and saw Kylie’s neck bent all wrong, bone sticking out — I couldn’t breathe, like the air just left my body.
I grabbed the metal bar and hit him — over and over — screaming, crying, his head splitting open while he moaned and reached for me.
I tore the planks off the door and threw it open, knowing he wanted me—this was the only way to lead Bill to him, even if it got me killed.

I stood there, staring at the ground, tears in my eyes, and motioned for Bill to run without me. I didn’t look up at the diseased people closing in, but I could hear their raspy breathing and their screams—so many voices, all full of rage, all aimed at me.

They grabbed me, touched me, pulled at my clothes—I trembled and said I was sorry, that I hadn’t behaved how he wanted. Then I choked out that we needed to talk, but not like this, not through all of them—I wanted to speak to his real face, Grant’s true self.
I stood in my front yard and looked up—my house wasn't mine anymore. They'd torn the wall open, thrown up some crooked wood, and the roof sagged like it was ashamed to still be standing.
I saw the meat thermometer on the floor, snapped off the top, and hid the metal spike in my skirt—sharp enough to use if I had to.
The song we danced to started playing through the walls—'Every Woman in the World'—and when I looked up through the broken ceiling, I saw a sliver of him and called out, 'Grant? We should talk.'
I touched his tentacle, my fingers were trembling, and when he pulled away and growled, I still reached for him again—because I had to make him see that I meant it, that I brought Bill for him.
I said, 'See? I brought him here for you! As an offering! To prove I love you more than him!' and smiled nervously, waiting for Grant to respond.
I reached out and touched his face—my skin crawled, stomach twisted—but I did it anyway, hand trembling as I made contact.
I was clutching my side, barely able to move, and when Bill tossed me the grenade, I reached for it—but I missed. It just hit the floor, and I couldn't get to it.
I threw the grenade behind him, clutching the pin so tight it cut into my palm, blood mixing with sweat as I let it go.

I crawled through the smoke, my hands burning on the floor, and looked down—what was left of the second floor was gone, and he was just... a pile of twitching flesh and things I didn’t recognize, no shape, no face, nothing like a man.
I came around the side of the house, pressing the paper towel roll against the cut on my ribs, and then I saw Bill—just standing there. I smiled at him, and he smiled back.
I felt the cold weight of the gun in my hand as I looked at Bill, tears streaming down my face, and when he said it was his nature, I told him this was mine—then I pulled the trigger.
I wiped the tears from my face, slid into the driver’s seat, and shoved the car into drive—I didn’t look back as I took off down the road, even though my body felt numb and the tears kept coming.
